metadata.case_name: LAM KAI v. NG KWOK LEUNG AND OTHERS

plaintiff.occupation_before: M.Phil student (Engineering) at the University of Hong Kong
plaintiff.occupation_after: Information Technology Officer and full time temporary teacher at Lai King Catholic Secondary School
plaintiff.education_level: Bachelor degree in Engineering; M.Phil (research) studies (incomplete)

source: The plaintiff was diagnosed to have suffered a severe head injury due to that collision.
A CT brain scan taken of the plaintiff showed diffuse cerebral contusion.
An MRI of the plaintiff's brain taken some six weeks later showed diffuse axonal damage.

injuries.description: truncal ataxia (failure of the muscles of the trunk)
source: Resulting from such head injury, the plaintiff suffers from headache, impairment of higher mental functions and truncal ataxia (i.e. failure of the muscles of the trunk).

manifestations.description: Lost consciousness at collision; remained unconscious for an unknown period but certainly for longer than the seven days when he was kept in the Intensive Care Unit of Tuen Mun Hospital.
Impairment of higher cognitive functions including concentration span, abstract thinking and possibly analytic power.
Post traumatic amnesia for some two months.
Truncal ataxia (failure of the muscles of the trunk).
Mild physical impairment (assessed as 3% of the whole person by Dr Brian Choa).
Depression and adjustment disorder with reduced self-confidence, social isolation and intermittent suicidal ideation related to losses from cognitive and functional impairments.

treatments_received: An operation was performed and an ICP monitor was inserted to monitor the intracranial pressure.
Occupational rehabilitation programme (attended until discharge four months after the accident)
Follow-up at neurosurgical clinic of Tuen Mun Hospital
Clinical psychology / psychological treatment (sessions with Ms Ide S.F. Chan of the Clinical Psychology Service, Tuen Mun Hospital)
treatments_future: Continuation of psychological treatment with Dr Ide Chan (Clinical Psychology Service) for approximately one to two years

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Unable to take part in volleyball and other sports at the level which the plaintiff used to and enjoyed before the accident.
